name: Steroidogenesis
summary: Cholesterol → every steroid hormone. StAR moving cholesterol into the mitochondrion is the true rate-limiting event; desmolase (CYP11A1) is the rate-limiting enzyme, driven by ACTH (adrenal) and LH (gonads). Columns follow the adrenal zones: glomerulosa (salt — aldosterone, angiotensin II), fasciculata (sugar — cortisol, ACTH), reticularis (sex — androgens, ACTH). Most enzymes are cytochrome P450s (NADPH + O₂).

dhea.name: DHEA
dhea.notes: Main adrenal androgen (with DHEA-S); weak on its own.

ohprog.name: 17α-Hydroxyprogesterone
ohprog.notes: ↑ in 21-hydroxylase deficiency — the newborn screening marker.

estrone.name: Estrone
estrone.notes: Main estrogen after menopause (made in adipose).

cortisol.name: Cortisol
cortisol.notes: Feeds back on ACTH. Low cortisol → ↑ ACTH → adrenal hyperplasia in CAH.

dht.name: Dihydrotestosterone
dht.notes: Drives external male genitalia, prostate growth, male-pattern baldness.

aldo.name: Aldosterone
aldo.notes: Zona glomerulosa only; driven by angiotensin II and K⁺, not much by ACTH.

cortisone.name: Cortisone
cortisone.notes: Inactive: it doesn't activate the glucocorticoid or mineralocorticoid receptor. Tissues switch cortisol off (11β-HSD2) or back on (11β-HSD1). Given as a drug, it works only after the liver converts it to cortisol (likewise prednisone → prednisolone).

chol.name: Cholesterol
chol.notes: From LDL uptake (mainly) or made in place; stored as cholesteryl esters.

doc.name: 11-Deoxycorticosterone
doc.notes: A weak mineralocorticoid — in excess (11β-hydroxylase or 17α-hydroxylase deficiency) it causes hypertension and hypokalemia.

star.name: StAR protein
star.notes: Moves cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane — the acute, rate-limiting event. Mutations → congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia.

scc.name: Desmolase
scc.notes: Rate-limiting enzyme. Stimulated by ACTH (adrenal) and LH (gonads). Inhibited by ketoconazole (also blocks 17,20-lyase).

hsd3b.name: 3β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
hsd3b.notes: Acts at three spots (pregnenolone, 17-OH-pregnenolone, DHEA). Deficiency: ↓ all three classes, salt wasting; ambiguous genitalia in both sexes.

cyp17h.name: 17α-Hydroxylase
cyp17h.notes: Deficiency: ↓ cortisol and sex hormones, ↑ DOC → hypertension, hypokalemia; XY undervirilized (female-appearing), XX lacks secondary sexual development. Abiraterone inhibits CYP17.

cyp17l.name: 17,20-Lyase
cyp17l.notes: Same CYP17A1 protein as 17α-hydroxylase. Inhibited by ketoconazole and abiraterone.

cyp21.name: 21-Hydroxylase
cyp21.notes: Most common CAH (>90%): ↓ cortisol and aldosterone, ↑ 17-OH-progesterone and androgens → salt wasting, hypotension, hyperkalemia, ↑ renin; virilized XX, precocious puberty in XY.

cyp11b1.name: 11β-Hydroxylase
cyp11b1.notes: Deficiency: ↓ cortisol and aldosterone but ↑ 11-deoxycorticosterone → hypertension and hypokalemia (↓ renin), plus virilization.

cyp11b2.name: Aldosterone synthase
cyp11b2.notes: Zona glomerulosa only; activated by angiotensin II and hyperkalemia.

hsd17b.name: 17β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
hsd17b.notes: Testes (Leydig cells) and ovary. Deficiency → undervirilized XY.

arom.name: Aromatase
arom.notes: Granulosa cells, adipose, placenta. Inhibitors (anastrozole, letrozole) treat ER+ breast cancer. Deficiency → maternal virilization in pregnancy.

srd5a.name: 5α-Reductase
srd5a.notes: Peripheral tissues (prostate, skin, hair follicles). Finasteride inhibits it (BPH, male-pattern baldness). Deficiency → ambiguous genitalia at birth, virilizing at puberty.

hsd11b2.name: 11β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2
hsd11b2.notes: Kidney (collecting duct), colon, salivary glands, placenta. Inactivates cortisol so it can't occupy the mineralocorticoid receptor, which binds cortisol as well as aldosterone. Blocked by glycyrrhetinic acid (black licorice), or absent (syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess) → hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, low renin and aldosterone. Very high cortisol (Cushing syndrome, ectopic ACTH) overwhelms it. In the placenta it shields the fetus from maternal cortisol.

hsd11b1.name: 11β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1
hsd11b1.notes: Liver, adipose tissue, brain: regenerates active cortisol from cortisone inside cells (NADPH comes from hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in the ER lumen). Why oral cortisone and prednisone work: they're activated here.

diffusion.name: Simple diffusion
diffusion.notes: Steroids are lipid-soluble: they cross mitochondrial and ER membranes (and leave the cell) without a carrier. Only cholesterol needs help into the mitochondria (StAR).

drugs.name: Ketoconazole
drugs.note: Blocks desmolase (and 17,20-lyase): Cushing syndrome; gynecomastia as a side effect.

diseases.name: 17α-Hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.clue: Hypertension and low potassium with no sex steroids: a phenotypic female with no puberty, or an XY person with female-appearing genitalia.

drugs.name: Abiraterone
drugs.note: Blocks CYP17 (17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), so no androgens from the adrenals: metastatic prostate cancer (given with prednisone).

drugs.name: Abiraterone
drugs.note: Blocks CYP17 (17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), so no androgens from the adrenals: metastatic prostate cancer (given with prednisone).

diseases.name: 17α-Hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.clue: Hypertension and low potassium with no sex steroids: a phenotypic female with no puberty, or an XY person with female-appearing genitalia.

drugs.name: Abiraterone
drugs.note: Blocks CYP17 (17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), so no androgens from the adrenals: metastatic prostate cancer (given with prednisone).

drugs.name: Abiraterone
drugs.note: Blocks CYP17 (17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), so no androgens from the adrenals: metastatic prostate cancer (given with prednisone).

diseases.name: 21-Hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.clue: Salt-wasting crisis (low Na⁺, high K⁺, hypotension) and ambiguous genitalia in a female newborn; raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone.

diseases.name: 21-Hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.clue: Salt-wasting crisis (low Na⁺, high K⁺, hypotension) and ambiguous genitalia in a female newborn; raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone.

diseases.name: 11β-Hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.clue: Virilization with hypertension and low potassium; raised 11-deoxycorticosterone and 11-deoxycortisol, low renin.

drugs.name: Metyrapone
drugs.note: Blocks 11β-hydroxylase: Cushing syndrome; the metyrapone test of ACTH reserve.

diseases.name: 11β-Hydroxylase deficiency
diseases.clue: Virilization with hypertension and low potassium; raised 11-deoxycorticosterone and 11-deoxycortisol, low renin.

drugs.name: Metyrapone
drugs.note: Blocks 11β-hydroxylase: Cushing syndrome; the metyrapone test of ACTH reserve.

diseases.name: 5α-Reductase deficiency
diseases.clue: XY child with ambiguous or female-appearing genitalia who virilizes at puberty; normal testosterone, low DHT.

drugs.name: Finasteride
drugs.note: Type 2 only: BPH, male-pattern hair loss.

drugs.name: Licorice
drugs.note: Glycyrrhetinic acid blocks 11β-HSD2, so cortisol acts on mineralocorticoid receptors: hypertension, hypokalemia (apparent mineralocorticoid excess).
